backlog.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3 so more of the 300 s is spent at peak LR. Keep FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0.
backlog.title: Lower warmdown ratio to 0.3

backlog.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the linear decay starts earlier in the time budget.
backlog.title: Higher warmdown ratio to 0.7

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18. This gives about twice as many optimizer steps in 300 s. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation drops to 2 micro-steps per step. Leave LRs unchanged at first.
backlog.title: Halve total batch size to 2**18

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17. Multiply MATRIX_LR by 0.8 and leave the other LRs unchanged. This tests very small batches, which give more steps in a short budget.
backlog.title: Total batch 2**17 with scaled LRs

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6. Keep ASPECT_RATIO at 64 and HEAD_DIM at 128. The smaller model sees more tokens in 300 s. If model_dim is not divisible by HEAD_DIM, adjust ASPECT_RATIO to 85 so that dim is 512.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider-step model

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 and keep ASPECT_RATIO 64. If DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 overflows, use 32 and let grad accumulation fill the rest. This tests whether the larger model pays off in 300 s.
backlog.title: Depth 10 model

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Lower WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.1

backlog.spec: Make the Muon weight decay follow the schedule: wd = WEIGHT_DECAY * (1 - progress), with progress being the elapsed time fraction. Update it each step in the training loop.
backlog.title: Linearly decaying weight decay

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.95).
backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 for a brief linear LR warmup.
backlog.title: Short warmup 3%

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not decay fully to zero.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "L". This uses full attention in all layers. The check is whether the throughput loss is repaid by better quality.
backlog.title: Window pattern all long

backlog.spec: Keep WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" but reduce the short window from half to a quarter of the sequence length. This should speed up the S layers. The last layer is forced to be long as before.
backlog.title: Window pattern SSSSL-like with shorter windows

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 so there are twice as many heads. Check that the flash attention kernel supports it, and that n_kv_head follows n_head.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: If the model applies a logit softcap, lower it to 15. If there is none, add logits = 15*tanh(logits/15) before the loss, computed in float.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 15

backlog.spec: Replace the ReLU^2 MLP with SwiGLU. Use hidden size about 8/3*dim, rounded to a multiple of 64, so parameters stay equal. Use three bias-free linear layers.
backlog.title: ReLU^2 MLP to SwiGLU at matched params

backlog.spec: Make sure the attention and MLP output projections (c_proj) are zero-initialized. If they already are, change the lm_head init std to 0.5 times the current value.
backlog.title: Zero-init residual projections check

backlog.spec: Lower SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 for the per-layer scalar parameters.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule to ramp from 0.85 to 0.97 over the first 200 steps, and hold 0.97 until warmdown. Hold it at 0.9 during the final 10% of training.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter/higher

backlog.spec: Reduce the Muon orthogonalization iterations from 5 to 4. This saves time per step. Keep the coefficients as they are.
backlog.title: Muon Newton-Schulz steps 4

backlog.spec: Compile the model with mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs". Compile time is not counted in the 300 s budget, but keep the total under 450 s. The check is whether throughput improves.
backlog.title: Disable torch.compile recompiles by mode max-autotune-no-cudagraphs

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before optimizer.step(). Do it after the accumulated backward passes.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: If the model has value embeddings on alternate layers, add them on every layer. If they are on every layer, restrict them to the last half of the layers. This trades parameters for speed.
backlog.title: Value embedding on alternate layers only

backlog.spec: Initialize the token embedding with std 0.5 instead of the current value, for example 1.0 to 0.5. Keep the other initializations the same.
backlog.title: Untie and shrink vocab-embedding init

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the parameters with decay 0.999, updated every step. Swap the EMA weights in before the final evaluation call only, without changing the evaluation code itself. Skip this if the swap cannot be done without touching the evaluation path.
backlog.title: Eval-time-style EMA of weights

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 and multiply EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR, MATRIX_LR and SCALAR_LR by about 0.7 (sqrt scaling). In a fixed 300 s budget, twice as many optimizer steps may beat the larger batch. Change only these constants.
backlog.title: Gradient accumulation-free smaller device batch with 2**18 total and sqrt-scaled LRs

backlog.spec: Make the number of gradient accumulation micro-steps depend on training progress. Use a total batch of 2**17 tokens for the first 30% of the time budget, 2**18 up to 60%, then 2**19 after that. Scale the loss per micro-step so that gradients are averaged correctly. Keep the LR schedule unchanged. This gives many cheap early steps and low-noise late steps.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp-up

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated every step after the first 100 steps, using torch._foreach_lerp_ for speed. Before the final evaluation call, copy the EMA weights into the model. Do not touch the evaluation call itself. Run the copy just before it. Combined with warmdown this may give a small gain. Remove it if it costs more than 1% in throughput.
backlog.title: Weight EMA used for evaluation

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH=12 and ASPECT_RATIO=48, so model_dim is 576. Check that it is divisible by HEAD_DIM. If not, use ASPECT_RATIO=43 so dim is about 512 and HEAD_DIM 128 divides it. Keep everything else the same. This tests whether a deeper and narrower model is better under a fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Smaller, deeper model: depth 12 at aspect ratio 48

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown of the LR multiplier with a cosine shape: for progress p in the warmdown phase, multiplier = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1-FINAL_LR_FRAC)*0.5*(1+cos(pi*(p-(1-WARMDOWN_RATIO))/WARMDOWN_RATIO)). Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5. Apply the same shape to the Muon momentum and weight-decay schedules only if they are already tied to the multiplier.
backlog.title: Cosine-shaped warmdown to zero

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule so it ramps from 0.85 to 0.97 over the first 600 steps instead of the current ramp, and hold 0.97 until the warmdown starts. Then lower it back to 0.9 across warmdown. Leave other optimizer settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon momentum 0.97 with Nesterov, longer warmup

backlog.spec: For the Muon matrix params, scale each layer's LR by a factor that goes linearly from 1.2 at the first layer to 0.8 at the last layer. Do this by creating a separate param group per layer, with its own LR scale that is multiplied by the schedule multiplier. This tests whether depth-dependent LRs help.
backlog.title: Per-layer learning-rate decay on the matrix LR

backlog.spec: Change the sequence length used in training (MAX_SEQ_LEN if the file defines it locally, otherwise the sequence length in the dataloader call) from the current value to half of it, and double the number of sequences per micro-batch to keep tokens per step the same. Shorter context makes attention cheaper, so more steps fit in 300 s. Verify the eval path still uses its own sequence length and do not alter it. If the length is imported from prepare.py and is not changeable, skip this and instead set WINDOW_PATTERN to 'SSSS' with the last layer forced full.
backlog.title: Token dropout-free data trick: pack with BOS-aligned shorter sequences

backlog.spec: In the attention module, add a gate: gate = sigmoid(linear(x[..., :32])) with a bias-free Linear(32, n_head) initialized to zero, giving 0.5 at the start. Multiply it by the attention output per head before the output projection, and scale by 2 so the initial value is 1. Add the gate weights to the matrix or Adam group with the scalar LR. This is a small, cheap architectural change that has helped in recent small-GPT speedruns.
backlog.title: Add learnable per-head attention output gate

backlog.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32, keeping TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE unchanged, so gradient accumulation doubles. This lowers peak memory and may raise throughput through better cache and allocator behavior. It is a pure systems change, so val_bpb should only move if tokens/s changes. Report the tokens processed in the 300 s run.
backlog.title: Compile with larger device batch via activation checkpointing off, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 32

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**16 (65536 tokens per step). Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 so gradient accumulation becomes 1 step if needed, and keep MATRIX_LR at 0.032, scaling EMBEDDING_LR and UNEMBEDDING_LR by 0.85. Smaller batches gave the largest gain so far, so this tests whether the trend continues.
backlog.title: Batch 2^16 with LR retune

backlog.spec: Make the per-step token count grow during training. For the first 30% of the time budget use TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**16, then switch to 2**17. Implement this by changing the number of gradient accumulation micro-steps (grad_accum_steps) from progress. Keep LRs unchanged and make sure the loop uses the current accumulation count when normalizing loss.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp-up

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown in the LR schedule function with a cosine shape: when progress is past the warmdown start, let t be the fraction through the warmdown and set the multiplier to FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1 - FINAL_LR_FRAC) * 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi * t)). Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown with FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.05

backlog.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR to 0.4 and UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.008 together. The small batch regime may prefer a lower embedding LR and a higher output-head LR. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4 and unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "L" so every layer uses full context attention. This tests whether the sliding windows are limiting quality. Check that the throughput loss is acceptable. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Window pattern all-long with half the layers

backlog.spec: Add a learnable gate to each attention layer: compute gate = sigmoid(Linear(first 32 dims of the layer input to n_head)) and multiply the per-head attention output by 2*gate before the output projection. Zero-initialize the gate weights so the gate starts at 1 (2*sigmoid(0)). Put the gate weights in the Muon matrix parameter group, or in the Adam scalar group if the shapes do not suit Muon.
backlog.title: Per-head sigmoid attention output gate

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 51 so model_dim is about 512 (round to a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128, which gives 512). The small batch regime handles more parameters better per token, so a model with more layers at the same width may do better. Keep the other hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Bigger model: depth 10 with aspect ratio 51

memo:
Helped: smaller batch size. Slot 8 (TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 131072, MATRIX_LR 0.032) scored 1.0516/1.0535 and was accepted, becoming the incumbent at 1.0558 mean_adjusted. It carries a tripwire flag, so audit it. Slot 13 (EMA scaffolding removed) scored 1.0510/1.0517/1.0510 (-0.0053) and was rejected, also with a tripwire. Its scores beat the incumbent, so check why it was rejected. Slot 12 (weight EMA) crashed.
Did not help: 2^18 batch with scaled LRs (+0.0383), DEPTH=12 (+0.0055), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0139), warmup 0.03 (+0.0159), weight decay 0.1 (+0.0015). Warmdown 0.7 (-0.0014), MATRIX_LR 0.05 (-0.0032) and SwiGLU (-0.0025) were all rejected. Those gains are probably within noise, since the incumbent has moved on.
Next: audit the tripwires first. Then try even smaller batches (65536) with LR retuning, and re-test SwiGLU on the new incumbent. Avoid more head or warmup changes.
